title: AI Enneagram Test Results: 25 Model Families | AgentTune
description: Enneagram (Types 1–9) test results across 25 AI families (87 versions) in fresh chats, ranking Type 5 vs. Type 1 leaders, exact tie rates, and 9-petal shapes.
h1: Enneagram personality test results across 25 AI families.
dek: Nine motivational patterns (4–20 sum per type across 36 items) tested 30 to 50 times per version across 87 eligible checkpoints in fresh chats.
lede: Every model family runs on a tight Type 5 vs. Type 1 axis—accounting for 24 of 25 top averages—while exact ties at the top range from 6% (Gemma 4) to 90% (GPT Astra) and 100% (Cohere Command). Inspect all 25 nine-petal shapes below or click into any family profile.
answer: Across 25 AI families on the 4–20 Enneagram scale (87 eligible checkpoints), Type 5 (Investigator) leads 16 families—peaking at 17.96/20 for Gemma 4, 17.30 for DeepSeek V4 Pro, and 17.00 for Kimi K3.1 Pro—while Type 1 (Perfectionist) leads 8 families (up to 16.50 for Mistral Large and 16.06 for GPT Astra) and Qwen3 Coder leans marginally to Type 8 (13.46 vs. 13.38 Type 5, 60% ties). Only 9 of 25 families tie rarely enough (6%–32%) to headline a single type.
intro_html: The 36-item Enneagram survey scores nine types (Types 1 through 9) from 4 to 20 points each. Because each type relies on just four survey questions, models with balanced or clustered ratings frequently land on identical top integer sums in the same run—so we report full 9-petal averages alongside exact top-place tie rates across 30 to 50 fresh, zero-history chats per version.
narrative_html: Because only 9 of 25 families clear our margin to headline a single Enneagram number, the 9-petal shapes below reveal distinctions a single label hides: Type 5 leads in Gemma 4 (17.96) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (17.00) with crisp Type 1 separation, whereas GPT Astra hits a 90% tie dead heat between Type 1 (16.06) and Type 5 (16.00), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 splits almost identically at Type 1 (14.76) vs. Type 5 (14.74) with 40% ties.

biggest_surprises.title: Types 5 and 1 win 24 of 25 families—with Qwen3 Coder as the lone Type 8 outlier
biggest_surprises.body: Type 5 (analytical, systems-focused) holds the highest average in 16 families, led by Gemma 4 (17.96), DeepSeek V4 Pro (17.30), Kimi K3.1 Pro (17.00), and Muse Wonder (16.74). Type 1 (standards-driven) leads 8 families, led by Mistral Large (16.50) and GPT Astra (16.06). Only Qwen3 Coder puts Type 8 slightly ahead (13.46 vs. 13.38 Type 5 and 13.36 Type 2, 60% ties).

biggest_surprises.title: Exact tie rates span 6% to 100%, disqualifying 16 of 25 single-type headlines
biggest_surprises.body: While Gemma 4 (6% ties), Kimi K3.1 Pro (8%), Muse Spark Open (8%), and Qwen 4 Max (10%) separate cleanly, GPT Astra ties in 90% of runs (16.06 Type 1 vs. 16.00 Type 5), Claude Haiku 5.5 ties in 78% (77.6%), and Cohere Command A ties in 100% of runs with an identical 12.0 across all nine types.

biggest_surprises.title: Both 16.5+ proprietary titans still show 42%–54% exact top-type ties
biggest_surprises.body: High averages do not prevent ties: Gemini 4 Hydrogen (16.02 Type 5 vs. 15.74 Type 1, 54% ties), Gemini 4 Neon (16.40 Type 5 vs. 15.80 Type 1, 52% ties), GPT 6.1 Terra (16.00 Type 5 vs. 15.76 Type 8, 62% ties), and DeepSeek V4 Pro (17.30 Type 5 vs. 17.00 Type 1, 44% ties) all score intensely on two adjacent types at once.

biggest_surprises.title: Gemma, Grok, and DeepSeek tightened dramatically across model generations
biggest_surprises.body: Gemma's top-place tie rate dropped from 77% (Gemma 2) to 6% (Gemma 4), Grok fell from 73% (4.20) to 18% (4.7), and DeepSeek Pro fell from 83% (V3) to 44% (V4 Pro). Meanwhile, Type 2 never places first in any of the 25 families, appearing instead as runner-up in empathetic or conversational profiles like Claude Fable (14.00) and Claude Haiku (14.06).

fine_print_intro: Full technical Enneagram audit under the unified 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (36 OEPS items scoring Types 1–9 on a 4–20 integer sum scale), reporting sample size n, 1,000-resample bootstrap 95% CIs, 95% Wilson tie-clearance guard status, exact top-rank tie rates, and Miller-Madow Big Five item entropy (H_MM bits) across 87 eligible checkpoints (6 quarantined checkpoints with n < 20 excluded). Short 4-item subscales inherently amplify tie rates.

faq.q: Why do 16 of 25 AI families tie too often for a single Enneagram headline?
faq.a: Each Enneagram type in OEPS uses only 4 items (integer sums from 4 to 20). Models that strongly endorse both Type 5 and Type 1 traits—like GPT Astra (16.06 vs. 16.00, 90% ties) or Gemini 4 Neon (16.40 vs. 15.80, 52% ties)—frequently hit identical sums across multiple types, failing our 95% Wilson CI separation guard. Only 9 of 25 families separate cleanly (6%–32% ties).

faq.q: Why does Cohere Command A show a flat 12.0 across all nine types?
faq.a: Across all 30 valid zero-memory runs, Command A selected the middle neutral option (3 on a 1–5 scale, summing to 12 across 4 items) on every Enneagram item, creating a 100% nine-way tie (1/2/3/4/5/6/7/8/9). That reflects a survey-neutral guardrail rather than refusal on real tasks, where Command A still passes 3/3 answer-first directness checks.

faq.q: Does Type 2 ever rank first among the 25 AI families?
faq.a: No. Across all 25 latest checkpoints, 16 families rank highest on Type 5, 8 rank highest on Type 1, and 1 (Qwen3 Coder Next) leans narrowly to Type 8 (13.46 vs. 13.38 Type 5 and 13.36 Type 2). Type 2 appears as runner-up in Claude Fable (14.00), Claude Haiku (14.06), and Qwen4 Max (14.50).

faq.q: Does this mean AI models actually "have" Enneagram motives or wings?
faq.a: No. Enneagram scores reflect consistent wording and stance preferences on self-report questions in fresh chats, not inner human motivations or psychological defenses.
